text: 17-year-old male. The patient was brought in by his mother for persistent bleeding following elective removal of wisdom teeth. The bleeding from the surrounding gums was minimally responsive to multiple gauze packs. The patient also has a history of easy bruising. Family history includes the patient's uncle who had similar issues with bleeding and a history of easy bruising and joint swelling.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that history; the family history of bleeding issues and joint swelling is particularly concerning for a clotting disorder. To confirm this, we need to see the results of the blood work I ordered. REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count, Coagulation_Profile results. REQUEST IMAGES: Any prior images showing joint swelling.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Hematologic tests show Hematocrit at 35%, Leukocyte Count at 8,500/mm3, and Platelet Count at 160,000/mm3. Coagulation profile reveals a Prothrombin Time of 15 sec, Partial Thromboplastin Time of 60 sec, and Bleeding Time of 6 min. Peripheral Blood Smear indicates normal-sized platelets, and Fibrin Split Products are negative. No prior images showing joint swelling were found in the system.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The blood work shows a normal platelet count and normal PT, but a significantly prolonged PTT (60 sec), which points toward an intrinsic pathway issue. Given your history of joint swelling and family history, have you ever experienced spontaneous bleeding into your joints or muscles?

REQUEST TEST: von_Willebrand_factor_assay
REQUEST TEST: Factor_VIII_activity

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: The requested tests for von Willebrand factor assay and Factor VIII activity are not included in the provided laboratory data; however, the available coagulation profile indicates a significantly prolonged Partial Thromboplastin Time (60 sec) with a normal Prothrombin Time (15 sec), consistent with an intrinsic pathway defect.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Hemophilia A. The clinical picture of a prolonged PTT, normal PT, normal platelet count, and a significant history of joint swelling (hemarthrosis) in the context of a family history of bleeding disorders is diagnostic for an intrinsic pathway factor deficiency, specifically Factor VIII.
